Usage: sim-remote [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:

  spawn          Run `simctl spawn` inside the simulator. With `--bin`, the binary is uploaded and run as argv[0]; otherwise the trailing args are the full in-simulator argv (e.g. `-- launchctl list`)

  setenv         Set a launchd environment variable inside the simulator (`launchctl setenv <key> <value>`)
  input          Send input events to a simulator
  reverse        Reverse-proxy TCP connections through a tunnel. Allows the simulator to access local TCP listeners through localhost
  forward        Forward a local port to a TCP listener on the remote host. The inverse of `reverse`: lets local tools reach a server running on the machine that hosts the simulator. Only servers started by your own session (your simulator's, your tooling's) are reachable
  login          Log in to sim-router and acquire a machine
  logout         Release the machine and forget the session
  acquire        Assign the current session a machine (no-op if it already has one)
  release        Release the current session's machine without logging out

  daemon         Control the background daemon
  install        Install a local `.app` on a simulator: the same as `sim-remote simctl install <UDID> <APP>`
  logs           Fetch a simulator's crash reports and logs
  moq-info       Print the MoQ relay URL and certificate fingerprint for a simulator
  install-shims  Write the Maestro/Appium shims and print the shell code that puts them on PATH, so a stock `maestro` CLI or Appium's XCUITest driver drives a remote simulator
